steps.title: Navigate to Settings
steps.detail: In the upper-right corner of any page on GitHub, click your profile picture, then click Settings.

steps.title: Open Developer settings
steps.detail: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings.

steps.title: Open OAuth apps
steps.detail: In the left sidebar, click OAuth apps.

steps.title: Start creating a new OAuth app
steps.detail: Click New OAuth App. If you haven't created an app before, this button will say, Register a new application.

steps.title: Enable device flow (optional)
steps.detail: If your OAuth app will use the device flow to identify and authorize users, click Enable Device Flow.

steps.title: Adjust token expiration setting
steps.detail: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default. If your app's authentication code hasn't been updated to support short-lived tokens, uncheck the box until support is added.

verification.expected: The provider shows its consent screen; after approval the browser lands on your redirect URI with a ?code= parameter.
A JSON response containing access_token (and refresh_token if you requested offline access).

blockers.cause: The code expired (10 minutes), was already exchanged, or belongs to another client.
blockers.fix: Restart the authorization redirect and exchange the new code once, immediately. Check the client ID matches the app that issued the code.

blockers.cause: Client ID or secret does not match the GitHub OAuth app.
blockers.fix: Copy the client ID and generate a new client secret in the same OAuth app; update both server-side values together.

blockers.symptom: redirect_uri_mismatch, or the provider says the redirect URI is not registered
blockers.cause: The callback URL sent in the request does not exactly match a registered redirect URI.
blockers.fix: Register the exact scheme, host, port and path in the provider console. No wildcards. Match the trailing slash. Use 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost if the provider is strict.

blockers.symptom: invalid_scope, or the consent screen omits a scope you requested
blockers.cause: The scope is not enabled for this app, is spelled differently, or was not granted by the user.
blockers.fix: Enable the scope in the provider console, request only configured scopes, then re-run consent. Check for read vs write variants.

blockers.cause: Client ID/secret pair is wrong, the secret was rotated, or a public client is sending a secret.
blockers.fix: Copy both values from the same app. Rotate the secret and redeploy. Public/native clients should use PKCE and no client secret.

blockers.cause: The user declined, is not an allowed test user, or the app is blocked by policy.
blockers.fix: Add the account as a test user, use the correct workspace, or complete the provider's app verification. Try an incognito window to avoid a stale session.

blockers.symptom: The token response has access_token but no refresh_token
blockers.cause: Offline access was not requested, consent was previously granted, or the provider only issues refresh tokens to certain client types.
blockers.fix: Request offline access (and a consent prompt if needed), revoke the app grant, then retry. Store the refresh token server-side.

blockers.symptom: invalid_grant with a PKCE verification error
blockers.cause: The code_verifier does not match the code_challenge, or the challenge was reused.
blockers.fix: Generate a fresh verifier per authorization request, use S256, keep it until the token exchange, and never reuse an authorization code.
